## Generic faults (any workload)

Network impairment (tc netem), outages (iptables, NetworkPolicy), resource stress and crashes, applied from an ephemeral container (`--tools-image`, default `nicolaka/netshoot:v0.16`) added to each target pod: it shares the pod's network namespace and cgroup, so only that pod is affected. Target pods with `target.namespace` + `target.podSelector` (or `graph`/`component` for Dynamo). Network impairment is egress: target a service's pods to slow its responses, its callers to slow their requests. One tc fault per pod at a time (enforced). Add `observe` to measure baseline / fault / recovery / after (see [docs/observability.md](docs/observability.md)).

### container-kill

Crash the main container (restart in place).

- **Effect:** Sends a signal to PID 1 of the pod's first container so it exits and restarts under its restartPolicy (restartCount increases); the pod, its IP and volumes stay. Unlike pod-kill this also works for bare pods such as KNE routers. The signal is sent from inside the container's PID namespace, where the kernel only delivers signals PID 1 handles: SIGKILL is always ignored there, so use a signal the app handles (most servers exit on TERM or INT). For an abrupt kill use pod-kill.
- **Recovery:** Nothing to revert; recovered when the pods are Ready again.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with process-namespace targeting (containerd 1.6+)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `signal` | `TERM` | TERM, INT, QUIT or HUP (must be one the app handles; KILL cannot reach PID 1 from inside the pod). |

```bash
simctl inject container-kill --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### cpu-stress

Burn CPU inside target pods.

- **Effect:** Busy workers in an ephemeral container share the pod's cgroup, competing with the workload for its CPU limit (throttling, higher latency) — a noisy neighbour or runaway thread.
- **Recovery:** The stress process is stopped (or ends after duration + 30s); recovered when the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `workers` | `1` | Busy processes. |
| `load` | `100` | Load per worker, percent. |

```bash
simctl inject cpu-stress --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### dependency-outage

Target pods can no longer reach a dependency.

- **Effect:** iptables rules in the pods reject (connection refused/reset) or drop (timeouts) traffic towards the destinations — a database, cache, model store or downstream service outage as the caller sees it.
- **Recovery:** The simulation's tagged iptables rules are removed; recovered when the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `destinations` | **required** | Comma-separated IPs, CIDRs, svc/<name> or svc/<namespace>/<name> the pods can no longer reach. |
| `ports` | — | Only these destination ports (comma-separated). |
| `protocol` | `tcp` | tcp, udp or all. |
| `mode` | `reject` | reject (fast failure: TCP reset / ICMP unreachable) or drop (silent: callers time out). |

```bash
simctl inject dependency-outage --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=api --param destinations=svc/postgres --param mode=drop --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### dns-outage

DNS resolution fails for target pods.

- **Effect:** Traffic to port 53 (UDP and TCP) from the pods is dropped or rejected, so name lookups time out or fail while existing connections keep working.
- **Recovery:** The tagged iptables rules are removed; recovered when the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `drop` | drop (lookups time out) or reject (fail fast). |
| `protocol` | `all` | Fixed to all (UDP and TCP). |
| `ports` | `53` | Fixed to 53. |

```bash
simctl inject dns-outage --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### memory-stress

Consume memory inside target pods.

- **Effect:** Allocates and touches memory in the pod's cgroup: page-cache pressure, then OOM kills if the pod's limit is exceeded (which process is killed is up to the kernel).
- **Recovery:** The allocation is released; recovered when the pods are Ready (after any OOM restarts).
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `size` | `256Mi` | Memory to allocate: bytes or with Mi/Gi/M/G. |

```bash
simctl inject memory-stress --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### net-bandwidth

Limit bandwidth.

- **Effect:** Egress is limited to the given rate; large responses (e.g. streamed tokens, model downloads) slow down and queues build. Applies to the pods' egress; to slow a service's responses, target the service's pods, to slow its callers' requests, target the callers.
- **Recovery:** `tc qdisc del dev <if> root` restores the default queueing; recovered when the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rate` | `1mbit` | Bandwidth limit, e.g. 1mbit, 512kbit. |
| `delay` | — | Added latency, e.g. 100ms. |
| `destinations` | — | Limit to traffic towards these: comma-separated IPs, CIDRs, svc/<name> or svc/<namespace>/<name>. Empty = all egress. |
| `ports` | — | Limit to these destination ports (comma-separated). |
| `interface` | `eth0` | Interface in the pod. |

```bash
simctl inject net-bandwidth --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --observe kubernetes --baseline 2m --after 2m --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/tc-netem.8.html>

### net-corruption

Corrupt a percentage of packets.

- **Effect:** Single-bit errors in packets; receivers drop them on checksum failure (looks like loss with retransmits). Applies to the pods' egress; to slow a service's responses, target the service's pods, to slow its callers' requests, target the callers.
- **Recovery:** `tc qdisc del dev <if> root` restores the default queueing; recovered when the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `corrupt` | `5` | Packets with a corrupted bit, percent. |
| `destinations` | — | Limit to traffic towards these: comma-separated IPs, CIDRs, svc/<name> or svc/<namespace>/<name>. Empty = all egress. |
| `ports` | — | Limit to these destination ports (comma-separated). |
| `interface` | `eth0` | Interface in the pod. |

```bash
simctl inject net-corruption --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --observe kubernetes --baseline 2m --after 2m --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/tc-netem.8.html>

### net-degraded

Combined impairment: latency, jitter, loss and bandwidth.

- **Effect:** Any combination of netem impairments in one fault, e.g. a congested WAN link. Applies to the pods' egress; to slow a service's responses, target the service's pods, to slow its callers' requests, target the callers.
- **Recovery:** `tc qdisc del dev <if> root` restores the default queueing; recovered when the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `delay` | — | Added latency, e.g. 100ms. |
| `jitter` | — | Latency variation (±), e.g. 20ms. |
| `correlation` | — | Jitter correlation with the previous packet, percent. |
| `distribution` | — | Jitter distribution: normal, pareto, paretonormal (empty = uniform). |
| `loss` | — | Packet loss, percent (e.g. 5 or 0.5). |
| `lossCorrelation` | — | Loss correlation (burstiness), percent. |
| `corrupt` | — | Packets with a corrupted bit, percent. |
| `duplicate` | — | Duplicated packets, percent. |
| `reorder` | — | Packets sent immediately (out of order), percent; needs delay. |
| `rate` | — | Bandwidth limit, e.g. 1mbit, 512kbit. |
| `destinations` | — | Limit to traffic towards these: comma-separated IPs, CIDRs, svc/<name> or svc/<namespace>/<name>. Empty = all egress. |
| `ports` | — | Limit to these destination ports (comma-separated). |
| `interface` | `eth0` | Interface in the pod. |

```bash
simctl inject net-degraded --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --param delay=80ms --param jitter=20ms --param loss=2 --param rate=10mbit --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/tc-netem.8.html>

### net-duplication

Duplicate a percentage of packets.

- **Effect:** Packets are sent twice; tests idempotency and duplicate handling of UDP protocols. Applies to the pods' egress; to slow a service's responses, target the service's pods, to slow its callers' requests, target the callers.
- **Recovery:** `tc qdisc del dev <if> root` restores the default queueing; recovered when the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `duplicate` | `5` | Duplicated packets, percent. |
| `destinations` | — | Limit to traffic towards these: comma-separated IPs, CIDRs, svc/<name> or svc/<namespace>/<name>. Empty = all egress. |
| `ports` | — | Limit to these destination ports (comma-separated). |
| `interface` | `eth0` | Interface in the pod. |

```bash
simctl inject net-duplication --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --observe kubernetes --baseline 2m --after 2m --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/tc-netem.8.html>

### net-jitter

Add variable latency (jitter).

- **Effect:** Packets get a random delay of delay ± jitter with the chosen distribution, so latency varies and packets may reorder. Applies to the pods' egress; to slow a service's responses, target the service's pods, to slow its callers' requests, target the callers.
- **Recovery:** `tc qdisc del dev <if> root` restores the default queueing; recovered when the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `delay` | `50ms` | Added latency, e.g. 100ms. |
| `jitter` | `40ms` | Latency variation (±), e.g. 20ms. |
| `correlation` | `25` | Jitter correlation with the previous packet, percent. |
| `distribution` | `normal` | Jitter distribution: normal, pareto, paretonormal (empty = uniform). |
| `destinations` | — | Limit to traffic towards these: comma-separated IPs, CIDRs, svc/<name> or svc/<namespace>/<name>. Empty = all egress. |
| `ports` | — | Limit to these destination ports (comma-separated). |
| `interface` | `eth0` | Interface in the pod. |

```bash
simctl inject net-jitter --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --observe kubernetes --baseline 2m --after 2m --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/tc-netem.8.html>

- **Effect:** A percentage of packets skip the delay and arrive before earlier ones. Applies to the pods' egress; to slow a service's responses, target the service's pods, to slow its callers' requests, target the callers.

| `reorderCorrelation` | `50` | Reorder correlation, percent. |
| `destinations` | — | Limit to traffic towards these: comma-separated IPs, CIDRs, svc/<name> or svc/<namespace>/<name>. Empty = all egress. |


### service-outage

A Service stops answering.

- **Effect:** A deny-all ingress NetworkPolicy on the Service's backend pods: every client sees the service as down (connections time out), while the pods themselves keep running and stay Ready.
- **Recovery:** The NetworkPolicy is deleted; recovered when it is gone and the backends are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`
- **Requires:** a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy (k3s does by default)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `service` | **required** | Service name (in target.namespace). |

```bash
simctl inject service-outage --target-namespace my-ns --param service=my-svc --probe-http http://my-svc.my-ns:8080/healthz --baseline 1m --after 1m --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

## GPU (Mokka mock NVML)

Injected with Mokka's `nvml-mock-ctl` in the `node-agent` container of the node's `nvml-mock` pod. Every mock-NVML consumer on the node (nvidia-smi, device plugin, GFD, dcgm-exporter, the Dynamo worker) sees the change within ~1s. Target a node (`target.node`, `target.nodeSelector`, default every Mokka node) and `target.gpu` (index, `all`, UUID; default `all`), **or** target pods (`target.graph`/`component`/`podSelector`) to hit exactly the GPUs those pods hold.

### gpu-clocks-degraded

SM/graphics clocks drop.

- **Effect:** Reported SM and graphics clocks are pinned to a low value, optionally with a P-state.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl reset --gpu` (clears every override on that GPU).
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mhz` | `300` | Clock in MHz. |
| `pstate` | — | Optional P-state 0-15 to report, e.g. 8. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-clocks-degraded --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-device-plugin-restart

Kill the NVIDIA device plugin.

- **Effect:** The node's nvidia.com/gpu capacity is re-registered with the kubelet; new GPU pods cannot schedule meanwhile, running pods keep their GPUs.
- **Recovery:** Recovered when the device plugin pod is Ready again.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** GPU Operator installed — the nvidia-sim gpuOperator component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gracePeriodSeconds` | `0` | Grace period for the delete; 0 is an abrupt kill (SIGKILL). |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-device-plugin-restart --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### gpu-ecc-uncorrectable

Uncorrectable (double-bit) ECC errors (Xid 48).

- **Effect:** The device stays addressable but uncorrectable ECC counters climb, with Xid 48 by default — the signal for retiring pages / draining the GPU.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl fail --mode healthy` removes the failure; recovered once nvidia-smi answers for the GPU. Kernel-log Xid lines are never retracted, as on real hardware.
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `xid` | `48` | Xid code surfaced through NVML events (and the kernel log when Mokka's nodeAgent.kernelLog is on). Empty for none. |
| `afterCalls` | — | Trip after N guarded NVML calls instead of immediately. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-ecc-uncorrectable --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>, <https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/>

### gpu-fabric-degraded

NVLink fabric health degraded.

- **Effect:** nvidia-smi -q Fabric → Health reports the given conditions (authoritative). Summary becomes Unhealthy / Limited Capacity.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl fabric-health --gpu <g> healthy`.
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component
- **Requires:** a GPU profile with an NVLink fabric (gb200, gb300)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `conditions` | `degraded_bandwidth` | Comma-separated: degraded_bandwidth, route_recovery, route_unhealthy, access_timeout_recovery, no_partition, insufficient_nvlinks, incompatible_gpu_fw, invalid_location, incorrect_sysguid, incorrect_chassis_sn, gpu_state_invalid. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-fabric-degraded --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-fallen-off-bus

GPU falls off the PCIe bus (Xid 79).

- **Effect:** Same NVML surface as lost, modelling a GPU that fell off the bus, with Xid 79 by default.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl fail --mode healthy` removes the failure; recovered once nvidia-smi answers for the GPU. Kernel-log Xid lines are never retracted, as on real hardware.
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `xid` | `79` | Xid code surfaced through NVML events (and the kernel log when Mokka's nodeAgent.kernelLog is on). Empty for none. |
| `afterCalls` | — | Trip after N guarded NVML calls instead of immediately. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-fallen-off-bus --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>, <https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/>

### gpu-lost

GPU becomes lost (NVML_ERROR_GPU_IS_LOST).

- **Effect:** Guarded NVML calls, handle lookups and event waits return GPU_IS_LOST. The device plugin marks the GPU unhealthy; pods using it typically fail health checks.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl fail --mode healthy` removes the failure; recovered once nvidia-smi answers for the GPU. Kernel-log Xid lines are never retracted, as on real hardware.
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `xid` | — | Xid code surfaced through NVML events (and the kernel log when Mokka's nodeAgent.kernelLog is on). Empty for none. |
| `afterCalls` | — | Trip after N guarded NVML calls instead of immediately. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-lost --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>, <https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/>

### gpu-memory-pressure

GPU framebuffer reported nearly full.

- **Effect:** memory.used/free are set so the GPU reports the given percent of its framebuffer in use (values are reported, nothing is allocated).
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl reset --gpu` (clears every override on that GPU).
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `usedPercent` | `95` | Percent of total memory reported used (0-100). |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-memory-pressure --gpu 0 --param usedPercent=97 --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-nvlink-errors

NVLink data-link errors climb.

- **Effect:** NVLink DL replay/recovery/CRC counters climb at the given rate on the GPU's active links (what DCGM_HEALTH_WATCH_NVLINK reads). Needs a profile with NVLink.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl nvlink-error --gpu <g> 0`.
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component
- **Requires:** a GPU profile with NVLink (h100, b200, gb200, gb300)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rate` | `100` | Errors per second. |
| `links` | — | Comma-separated link ids; empty = all active links. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-nvlink-errors --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-overheat

GPU overheats and thermally throttles.

- **Effect:** Reported GPU temperature is pinned high and, by default, the hw_thermal_slowdown throttle reason is raised. dcgm-exporter / alerting see the temperature and throttle.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl reset --gpu` returns the GPU to its profile (this clears every override on that GPU).
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `temperature` | `95` | Temperature in °C (0-200). |
| `throttle` | `true` | Also raise the thermal throttle reason. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-overheat --node $NODE --gpu 0 --param temperature=98 --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-power-throttle

GPU hits its power cap and throttles.

- **Effect:** Power draw is pinned (clamped to the profile's limits) and the sw_power_cap throttle reason raised; clocks can be pinned low too.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl reset --gpu` (clears every override on that GPU).
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `watts` | `700` | Reported power draw in W. |
| `clocksMHz` | — | Optionally pin SM/graphics clocks to this MHz. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-power-throttle --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-set

Write arbitrary mock NVML fields (escape hatch).

- **Effect:** Runs `nvml-mock-ctl set --gpu <g> key.path=value ...` for any field in Mokka's config schema; unknown fields are rejected by nvml-mock-ctl.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl reset --gpu` (clears every override on that GPU).
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fields` | **required** | Comma-separated key.path=value pairs, e.g. "ecc.mode_current=false,pstate=8". |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-set --gpu 0 --param fields=pstate=8 --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>, <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/configuration.md>

### gpu-sram-ecc

On-die SRAM ECC errors.

- **Effect:** ecc.sram counters (volatile and aggregate) report the given count; optionally raises SRAM Threshold Exceeded, the driver's 'needs servicing' signal.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl sram-ecc --gpu <g> 0`.
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `count` | `4` | Error count. |
| `type` | `secded` | correctable, parity or secded. |
| `source` | `sm` | Unit for uncorrectable errors: l2, sm, microcontroller, pcie, other. |
| `thresholdExceeded` | `true` | Raise SRAM Threshold Exceeded. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-sram-ecc --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-throttle

Set active clock-throttle reasons.

- **Effect:** nvidia-smi / NVML report the given clocks_throttle_reasons (authoritative: other reasons cleared).
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl throttle --gpu <g> none`.
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `reasons` | `thermal` | Comma-separated: thermal, sw_thermal, power, power_brake, hw_slowdown, sync_boost, idle, app_clocks, display_clocks. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-throttle --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-utilization

Pin GPU and memory utilization.

- **Effect:** GPU and memory utilization report a fixed percent (e.g. 100 for a saturated GPU, 0 for an idle one). Useful for autoscaling and alerting tests.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl reset --gpu` (clears every override on that GPU).
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `percent` | `100` | Utilization 0-100. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-utilization --graph mocker-agg --component decode --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>

### gpu-xid

Raise a GPU Xid error with a chosen failure mode.

- **Effect:** The GPU trips the chosen failure mode and NVML delivers the Xid event; device plugin / DCGM / health monitors react as to a real Xid.
- **Recovery:** `nvml-mock-ctl fail --mode healthy` removes the failure; recovered once nvidia-smi answers for the GPU. Kernel-log Xid lines are never retracted, as on real hardware.
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `gpu`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `namespace`, `count`
- **Requires:** Mokka (nvml-mock) installed — the nvidia-sim mokka component

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `ecc_uncorrectable` | Failure mode: ecc_uncorrectable, lost or fallen_off_bus. |
| `xid` | **required** | Xid code surfaced through NVML events (and the kernel log when Mokka's nodeAgent.kernelLog is on). Empty for none. |
| `afterCalls` | — | Trip after N guarded NVML calls instead of immediately. |

```bash
simctl inject gpu-xid --graph mocker-agg --component decode --param xid=43 --param mode=lost --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-test-infra/blob/main/docs/nvml-mock-ctl.md>, <https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/>

## Dynamo

Faults aimed at the Dynamo inference graph. With no target they default to the graph `mocker-agg` in namespace `nvidia-sim` (controller flags `--default-graph`, `--default-graph-namespace`); set `target.graph`/`target.namespace` for another graph.

### dynamo-frontend-isolate

Partition the frontend.

- **Effect:** Clients cannot reach the frontend (ingress) and/or the frontend cannot reach workers (egress).
- **Recovery:** NetworkPolicy deleted; recovered when the frontend is Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy (k3s does by default)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `both` | ingress, egress or both. |
| `allowDNS` | `true` | Keep DNS (port 53) egress open so only service traffic is cut. |

```bash
simctl inject dynamo-frontend-isolate --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### dynamo-frontend-kill

Kill the Dynamo frontend pod(s).

- **Effect:** The OpenAI-compatible endpoint goes away until the operator recreates the frontend, which then rediscovers workers.
- **Recovery:** Recovered when as many frontend pods are Ready as before.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gracePeriodSeconds` | `0` | Grace period for the delete; 0 is an abrupt kill (SIGKILL). |

```bash
simctl inject dynamo-frontend-kill --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/latest/kubernetes/fault-tolerance/overview>

### dynamo-operator-restart

Kill the Dynamo operator.

- **Effect:** DynamoGraphDeployments stop being reconciled until the operator is back; running graph pods are unaffected.
- **Recovery:** Recovered when the operator pod is Ready again.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gracePeriodSeconds` | `0` | Grace period for the delete; 0 is an abrupt kill (SIGKILL). |

```bash
simctl inject dynamo-operator-restart --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### dynamo-worker-isolate

Partition the decode workers from the frontend and control plane.

- **Effect:** Requests routed to the worker time out; with egress cut the worker also loses Kubernetes discovery and is dropped from routing (Dynamo's FRONTEND_WORKER partition).
- **Recovery:** NetworkPolicy deleted; recovered when the workers are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy (k3s does by default)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `both` | ingress, egress or both. |
| `allowDNS` | `true` | Keep DNS (port 53) egress open so only service traffic is cut. |

```bash
simctl inject dynamo-worker-isolate --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/knowledge-base/concepts/fault-tolerance/fault-tolerance-testing>

### dynamo-worker-kill

Kill Dynamo decode worker pod(s).

- **Effect:** The worker disappears mid-flight; in-flight requests fail or migrate (frontend --migration-limit), the router drops the worker, the operator recreates the pod and it re-registers.
- **Recovery:** Recovered when the graph has as many Ready worker pods as before.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gracePeriodSeconds` | `0` | Grace period for the delete; 0 is an abrupt kill (SIGKILL). |

```bash
simctl inject dynamo-worker-kill --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/latest/kubernetes/fault-tolerance/overview>, <https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/kubernetes/fault-tolerance/request-migration>

## Kubernetes

Generic faults for any workload.

### node-cordon

Cordon nodes.

- **Effect:** Nodes become unschedulable; combine with a kill to see replacement pods stay Pending (on a single node the whole env).
- **Recovery:** Nodes this simulation cordoned are uncordoned (nodes already cordoned are left alone).
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `count`

```bash
simctl inject node-cordon --node $NODE --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### pod-kill

Kill pods matching a selector.

- **Effect:** Deletes the matched pods (abruptly by default). Their controller replaces them.
- **Recovery:** Nothing to revert; recovered when as many matching pods are Ready as before the kill.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gracePeriodSeconds` | `0` | Grace period for the delete; 0 is an abrupt kill (SIGKILL). |

```bash
simctl inject pod-kill --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

## Network

NetworkPolicy partitions, and link faults for emulated networks (the [network-kne environment](../../environments/network-kne/README.md)): take router interfaces down or flap them; combine with `net-*` faults on a router interface (`--param interface=eth1`) for degraded links.

### link-down

Take a pod interface (e.g. a router link) down.

- **Effect:** ip link set <interface> down in the pod: for KNE routers the link to the neighbour goes down, so routing protocols (BGP/IS-IS/OSPF) drop the adjacency and reconverge.
- **Recovery:** ip link set <interface> up; recovered when the pods are Ready (check protocol state with probes).
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `interface` | **required** | Interface to take down, e.g. eth1 (KNE link). |

```bash
simctl inject link-down --target-namespace kne-2node-xrd --pod-selector app=r1 --param interface=eth1 --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### link-flap

Flap a pod interface down/up repeatedly.

- **Effect:** The interface goes down for downSeconds and up for upSeconds in a loop — route flap dampening, BFD/hold timers and convergence under churn.
- **Recovery:** The loop stops and the interface is left up.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** ephemeral containers with NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW (blocked by the restricted/baseline Pod Security profiles)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `interface` | **required** | Interface to flap, e.g. eth1. |
| `downSeconds` | `5` | Seconds down per cycle. |
| `upSeconds` | `20` | Seconds up per cycle. |

```bash
simctl inject link-flap --target-namespace kne-2node-xrd --pod-selector app=r1 --param interface=eth1 --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

### network-isolate

Cut pods off the network with a NetworkPolicy.

- **Effect:** A deny-all NetworkPolicy for the matched pods (ingress, egress or both; DNS kept by default).
- **Recovery:** The NetworkPolicy is deleted; recovered when it is gone and the pods are Ready.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy (k3s does by default)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `both` | ingress, egress or both. |
| `allowDNS` | `true` | Keep DNS (port 53) egress open so only service traffic is cut. |

```bash
simctl inject network-isolate --target-namespace my-ns --pod-selector app=my-app --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

## Measurement only

No fault: measure baseline / during / after around your own action. See [docs/observability.md](docs/observability.md).

### observe-only

Measure a window without injecting anything.

- **Effect:** Nothing is changed. With spec.observe, the baseline / "fault" / after windows are measured around whatever happens meanwhile — run your own action (deploy, load test, failover) while it is Active, then recover it.
- **Recovery:** Nothing to revert; recovered immediately when duration elapses or recovery is requested.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`

```bash
simctl inject observe-only --target-namespace my-ns --observe kubernetes --baseline 5m --after 5m --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

## Run:ai (runai-sim)

For the [runai-sim environment](../../environments/runai-sim/README.md): KWOK virtual GPU nodes (fake-gpu-operator) scheduled by KAI Scheduler. `pod-kill`, `network-isolate` and `node-cordon` work there too (target `--node-selector type=kwok` / the workload pods); GPU-through-Mokka and `dynamo-*` types do not apply to virtual nodes.

### fgo-gpu-utilization

Change the GPU utilization fake-gpu-operator reports for pods.

- **Effect:** Sets run.ai/simulated-gpu-utilization on the matched pods, so FGO's synthetic DCGM metrics report that utilization range — e.g. idle GPUs for idle-reclaim / consolidation tests or saturated ones for alerting and autoscaling.
- **Recovery:** Each pod's previous annotation value is restored (or removed). Pods recreated by their controller get the template's value anyway.
- **Targets:** `namespace`, `podSelector`, `graph`, `component`, `count`
- **Requires:** runai-sim environment (fake-gpu-operator)

| Param | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `range` | `95-100` | Percent N or range N-M, e.g. 0 or 95-100. |

```bash
simctl inject fgo-gpu-utilization --target-namespace runai-sim --pod-selector app=train-whole-gpu --param range=0 --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://github.com/run-ai/fake-gpu-operator>

### kwok-node-down

A virtual GPU node fails (stops heartbeating).

- **Effect:** The KWOK heartbeat stops, so the node goes NotReady after the node-monitor grace period (~40s) and gets the unreachable taint; its pods are evicted after their not-ready toleration (default 300s) and KAI Scheduler must place them elsewhere. GPUs on the node drop out of the queues' available capacity.
- **Recovery:** The KWOK heartbeat resumes; recovered when the nodes are Ready again (re-scheduling of evicted workloads is up to their controllers and KAI).
- **Targets:** `node`, `nodeSelector`, `count`
- **Requires:** runai-sim environment (KWOK virtual nodes); real nodes are refused

```bash
simctl inject kwok-node-down --node-selector run.ai/simulated-gpu-node-pool=h100 --count 1 --duration 2m --wait recovered
```

References: <https://kwok.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/kwok-manage-nodes-and-pods/>, <https://github.com/kai-scheduler/KAI-Scheduler>
